content: Before inserting an image into a chapter on WikiDoc, it is mandatory to first upload the image to the WikiDoc server. Images can only be embedded into a WikiDoc page if they have been successfully uploaded to the server, which is the system responsible for hosting and serving all the pages you view. If the image you wish to use is not yet on the server, you must upload it. This process involves navigating to the upload page, which can be accessed by clicking Upload file or searching for Special:Upload on WikiDoc. The upload page provides detailed instructions for adding or uploading an image to the server. On the Upload file page, you will encounter two fields. In the field labeled Source file name, you need to click the gray Browse button to locate the file on your computer's hard drive that you wish to upload. In the field labeled Destination file name, you must type the name you want the image to have on WikiDoc. It is crucial to use a descriptive name for the image so that it can be easily found and cataloged by search engines. This point cannot be overstated: the file name should resemble a search criterion you would use to locate the image via a search engine's image function. Once you have completed these steps, click the Upload file button. After the upload is complete, the image will appear on the server. It is recommended to copy the file name of the uploaded image so that you can easily insert it into the desired WikiDoc page. Once an image has been uploaded to the server, it can be inserted into any number of pages. You can find the file names of uploaded images in the Image file list on WikiDoc. Knowing the file name is essential for inserting the image. Additionally, you can view uploaded images in the Gallery of new images. To insert an image into a WikiDoc page, you must use image code. This is done by typing a specific line of code in the editing window of the page you are working on. To access the editing panel, select the Edit this page tab at the top of the page. Ensure you are signed in so that your contributions are properly credited. Before placing the code, carefully consider the optimal placement of the image. This often involves thinking about how the text will wrap around the image. For instance, it may look best if the image aligns with the start of a section. If this is the case, create an empty line immediately under or above the heading, depending on what looks better, and type the image code. The extra line will not affect the final output apart from producing the image. After inserting the code, press the Show preview button at the bottom of the editing window to see how the reformatted page will look. If the image is placed on the left or right, the text will wrap around the image from the top of the section. If the image is centered (or no alignment is specified), the text will not wrap, and it will appear below the image. If the result is not as expected, you can adjust the text and code as many times as necessary until it looks correct. Once satisfied, press the Save page button at the bottom of the page. Most images on the WikiDoc server are too large to display at their full size. In nearly all cases, image reduction is required. The server also needs to know where to place the image and whether a frame or caption is needed. With these common requirements in mind, it is recommended to use a standard format that includes all the basic options. Examples of commonly used syntax are provided in the Examples section below. For image formatting, the following options are available: 1. Thumbnail or Thumb: The image is scaled down to a standard width (default is 180 pixels) and surrounded by a box. If a caption is provided, it appears below the image. By default, the image is placed on the right unless overridden with a location attribute. 2. Frame: The original image size is preserved, and a box is added around the image. If a caption is provided, it appears below the image. 3. No specification: The original image size is preserved, and no border is added. If a caption is provided, it is not displayed. 4. Border: Similar to no specification, but a border is added around the image. For image placement, the following options are available: 1. Right: The image, including its box, is placed on the right side of the page, and the text flows around it. 2. Left: The image, including its box, is placed on the left side of the page, and the text flows around it. 3. Center: The image, including its box, is centered on the page, and the text appears below it. 4. None: The image, including its box, is placed on the left side of the page, and the text appears below it. For image size, you can specify dimensions such as 100px to scale the image to a width of 100 pixels. If you specify both width and height (e.g., 100x200px), the image will be scaled proportionally to fit within these dimensions while maintaining its original aspect ratio. Captions can be added to provide additional context or description for the image. Any text that does not match a recognized option is assumed to be caption text. The new advanced syntax for inserting images is backward compatible, meaning existing articles do not need to be modified. This syntax allows for various options to control the placement, size, and presentation of the image. Options can be combined and separated by vertical bars (|). Unrecognized options are treated as caption text, but this typically applies only if thumbnail is specified. For galleries or multiple images, specific markup can be used to display images in a grid-like format. Additional formatting options are available to align galleries to the left or right and allow text to flow around them. For example, images of arterioles can be displayed side by side for comparison, with captions describing their characteristics, such as normal arterioles, hypertensive arterioles with wall thickening, and arterioles in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) patients with perivascular fibrosis. These visual comparisons can highlight differences in wall-to-lumen ratios, subendocardial ischemia, and impaired coronary flow reserve.
